cards.name: EMP Drone
cards.flavor: No signal. No abilities. No complaints: nobody can call to complain.
cards.notes: Jamming Field (Pokémon's Neutralizing Gas): every other creature's ability is switched off while it stands, on either side. Yours too.
cards.picture: A quadcopter drone hovering over the battlefield emitting concentric rings of static, every creature below holding a phone with no bars, their glowing ability icons flickering out one by one.

cards.name: Buffering
cards.notes: Trend for 3 Days (Trick Room, Tech's flavour): Rush Hour, the slowest act first.
cards.picture: A battlefield frozen under a giant spinning loading wheel, every creature caught mid-leap with a BUFFERING 99% label, the one dial-up modem in the corner going first.

cards.name: Web Scraping
cards.flavor: We respect your robots.txt. We read it, anyway.
cards.notes: Tech's scouting: send for any card among the top 5 of your deck; it joins your next hand.
cards.picture: A cat scratching at a laptop screen, claw marks tearing the web page open and spilling out cards and data.

cards.name: DDOS Attack
cards.flavor: Ten thousand requests a second. All of them from fridges.
cards.notes: 2 damage, and Exhausted: it cancels the target's planned actions (spells land before attacks), lasts the rest of the Day and all of the next, turns its abilities off and adds +1 to every hit (Exposed). Aimed at an enemy slot it's Fixed: the enemy can dodge by moving.
cards.picture: A server rack melting under an avalanche of tiny envelope icons, smart fridges and toasters in the background, each with a red glowing eye.

cards.name: Antivirus
cards.flavor: 1 threat blocked. 37 offers to upgrade to Premium.
cards.notes: Mechanics test: a Watchdog (GDD 3.11). It's created when the spell resolves and, Monitored, nullifies the next enemy spell before it resolves, even one planned before it existed. 1 charge.
cards.picture: A panda in shining knight's armor, an antivirus logo on its shield, blocking a glowing spell scroll at a castle gate, while the castle walls behind it are plastered with its own pop-ups: "RENEW NOW - 60% OFF".

cards.name: Script Kiddie
cards.flavor: Doesn't know how it works. Doesn't need to.
cards.notes: Mechanics test: Zero-Day. Its attacks and effects ignore the target's defensive abilities (Unbothered, No U, Return to Sender...), except Cold Storage.
cards.picture: A twelve-year-old in an oversized gaming chair, hoodie up, double-clicking "H4CK3R T00L.exe" while a bank vault door swings open on his second monitor.

cards.name: Legacy Code
cards.flavor: Written in 1987. Nobody knows how it works. Nobody dares touch it.
cards.notes: Mechanics test: Cold Storage. Enemy effects can't lower its stats, and Zero-Day can't get around it.
cards.picture: A beige mainframe held together with duct tape in a dusty basement, a yellowed sticky note on it: "DO NOT TOUCH - Gary (retired 1999)", and cobwebs over an "Update available" pop-up.

cards.name: End-to-End Encryption
cards.flavor: Not even we can read your messages. Pinky promise.
cards.notes: Mechanics test: Encrypted for 2 Days on a friendly creature. Watchdogs ignore its actions and spend no charge on them.
cards.picture: Two carrier pigeons passing a sealed envelope covered in padlocks, while a government agent below swings a butterfly net and waves a "Backdoor Request" form.

cards.name: SysAdmin
cards.flavor: Have you tried turning it off and on again?
cards.notes: Each Dawn it cleanses your creatures' statuses, all of them (Tech owns Cleanse; since 2026-10-15 a Cleanse takes the good ones too).
cards.picture: A bearded sysadmin in socks and sandals yanking the power cable out of a smoking server rack, a coffee mug in his other hand.

cards.name: Meatproxy As A Service
cards.flavor: Powered by AI. The AI is Dave. Dave copies and pastes.
cards.notes: A draw each Dawn, paid with 1 of your Health. Future: Technical Debt (fewer draws next Day).
cards.picture: A raw steak sitting at a desk, copy-pasting text from one window to another on a computer screen, a price tag on the monitor: $9.99/MONTH.

cards.name: Ransomware Attack
cards.flavor: Your files are safe. With us.
cards.notes: Exhausted, 2 damage, and you draw a card (the ransom).
cards.picture: A computer screen with a grinning skull and a padlock demanding 1 BTC, while a grandma cries into her knitting.

cards.name: Man-in-the-Middle
cards.flavor: Hi, it's your bank. Also, it's not.
cards.notes: A Monitored Watchdog: the next enemy spell is redirected to a random creature. 1 charge.
cards.picture: A man squeezed on a park bench between two lovers, holding both of their phones and reading their texts.

cards.name: Technical Debt
cards.flavor: Ship it now. Someone will fix it later. You are someone.
cards.notes: Decay 1: strong today, it pays for it every Dusk.
cards.picture: A laptop held together with duct tape and a TODO sticky note, beside an empty, cracked piggy bank, the dashed outlines of the missing banknotes floating above.

cards.name: Scope Creep
cards.flavor: Just one more small feature. And one more.
cards.notes: Grow 1: it gets bigger every Dawn, like the project.
cards.picture: A Gantt chart on an office whiteboard whose bars have outgrown it: they run off the board, across the wall and out of the window, past the DEADLINE line drawn in red, while a smiling manager sticks on one more note: "+1 small feature".

cards.name: Sex Clanker
cards.flavor: Batteries not included. Feelings not included either.
cards.notes: Arrival: Heat Signature 3 on itself. It draws every random effect and redirected attack: a decoy too attractive to ignore.
cards.picture: Candlelight and satin: a figure in full shining plate reclines on a red heart-shaped bed, propped on one elbow, a rose in the visor and one knee up, rose petals everywhere, a heart shield leaning against the bed.

cards.name: Threat Hunter
cards.flavor: Assume breach. Then go looking for it.
cards.notes: Homing (the user, 2026-10-16): its attacks lock on the enemy creature in the slot it's aimed at and follow it if it moves. Arrival: Heat Signature 1 on a random enemy creature, which then pulls every Homing effect, its own included: aim at anything and the hottest one takes it. Tech's Heat and Homing in one card.
cards.picture: A security analyst in a headlamp crawling on hands and knees through a tunnel of server cables with a magnifying glass, following a trail of glowing red footprints to a tiny hooded hacker hiding behind a rack.

cards.name: Ctrl + Z
cards.flavor: Undo. Undo. Undo. Undo the undo.
cards.notes: A friendly creature goes back to your hand (with the next Day's hand), and you draw 1 more next Day. Played again, its Arrival happens again, and it comes back fresh: a reset for a hurt creature, a second Arrival for one with a good one (Threat Hunter, Sex Clanker). Unlike Shadow Ops.' Extraction, no new face, a card instead.
cards.picture: A huge curved UNDO arrow pulling a startled knight backwards off a battlefield into a playing card held up by a hand, the keys CTRL and Z glowing on a keyboard below.

cards.name: Pair Programming
cards.flavor: One types, one watches. Both bill the hours.
cards.notes: A swapper: target friendly creature trades places with its partner in the formation, then it and the creatures beside it where it lands get +1 Attack this Day. Lines up a pair on one lane, or pulls a hurt creature out of one.
cards.picture: Two developers squeezed at one tiny desk sharing a single keyboard: one types with a coffee in his other hand, the other leans over his shoulder pointing at a bug on the screen, a timesheet pinned between them billing 16 hours.

cards.name: Suspicious USB Stick in the Parking Lot
cards.flavor: SALARIES 2026. Do not open. Definitely open.
cards.notes: A Gift (Stuxnet reportedly got into Iran's nuclear plant on USB sticks): you play it into an empty enemy slot and it joins their side. On arrival, a random other creature of its new side is Exhausted (infected), and it carries Heat Signature 1, pulling their random effects and your Homing ones.
cards.picture: A lone USB stick lying on the asphalt of an empty parking lot under a streetlight, labelled SALARIES 2026 in marker, an employee in a lanyard bending down to pick it up, a nuclear plant's cooling tower behind the fence.

cards.name: Code Review
cards.flavor: LGTM. (Didn't read it.)
cards.notes: The sweeper (Rapid Spin, Defog): clears the Slot Effects on every one of your slots (Border Crossing, Landmines, Scorched Earth), and you draw a card next Day.
cards.picture: Two developers at a desk, one pointing at a screen full of red warning markers, the other shrugging and clicking 'Approve' with a coffee in hand.

cards.name: Bomber Drone
cards.flavor: Delivered in 30 minutes, or your village is free.
cards.notes: Hit and Run: after its attack it goes back to your hand, fresh, with the next Day's. It strikes and is gone before the answer comes.
cards.picture: A quadcopter drone with a delivery company's logo dropping a small bomb on a tank and zipping away, a 5-star rating popping up on its operator's phone below.

cards.name: Ctrl + Y
cards.flavor: Redo. And again. And again.
cards.notes: Combo: 1 damage to target creature or player, 1 more for each other spell you play this Day. Tech's spells pile up into a finisher.
cards.picture: A keyboard with the Y key worn down to a nub, a hand mashing Ctrl + Y while the same explosion repeats on the screen behind it.
